title: Reviewing a contract before accepting the work
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Operations managers, estimators and supervisors who review service contracts or tenders before work is accepted.
learningOutcomes: Set out the client requirements in writing before costing a contract.
Use a contract check sheet covering time frames, staffing, pricing, payment terms and escalation.
Explain why an unpriced staffing or time requirement puts the margin at risk.

instruction.heading: Understanding the requirement
instruction.body: The sample firm requires the operations manager to read every enquiry, to confirm the contact person and to resolve any unclear requirement with the client in writing before costing. Client documents and confidential information remain the business's responsibility until handed back to the client. A requirement that is not written down is a requirement that cannot be priced or defended.

instruction.heading: Costing and the decision to tender
instruction.body: The operations manager prices the chemicals, consumables, labour hours and kit, and prepares a cost-benefit comparison for the head of the business. The directors then decide whether the company has the skills and funds to meet the client's needs and finish the work well. Only then is the tender drafted, verified for correctness and sent.

instruction.heading: The contract check sheet
instruction.body: When a contract is awarded, the operations manager compares the tender with the signed contract. The sample's review covers the schedule windows, the number of workers needed, the price, when and how payment is made, the rules for raising prices mid-contract, and any capital outlay. A filled-in sheet is the proof that the review happened. A price that does not cover the staffing the contract requires will erode the hourly rate of every job under it, so check the labour hours against the price before signing.

procedure: Collect the client's requirements in writing, including the contact person and the standards that apply.
Cost the labour hours, chemicals, consumables and equipment for the scope.
Prepare the cost-benefit analysis and get the approval the business requires before tendering.
When awarded, compare the tender with the contract and complete the contract check sheet.
Check that the staffing in the contract matches the labour hours in the costing.
File the signed checklist with the contract.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial office tender asks for a three-person crew each evening for five evenings. The costing allows two people for four hours each night.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the reviewer check before signing, and what decision is made if the costing is short?
workedExamples.reasoning: The reviewer compares the staffing in the contract with the labour hours in the costing, and sees the gap. The reviewer returns the costing for revision and the decision on price or staffing goes to the head of the business before the contract is signed.

equipmentAndPpe: Client requirement document, costing sheet, tender copy, signed contract and the contract check sheet.

commonErrors.error: Signing a contract whose staffing has not been costed.
commonErrors.prevention: Compare the contract's staffing with the labour hours before signing.
Get every requirement confirmed in writing.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out escalation clauses and payment terms.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the full checklist every time.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Contract terms on insurance, licensing and the client's own safety rules must be checked against the business's obligations.

qualityStandard: The checklist is complete and signed before the contract is accepted.
The contract staffing and the costed labour hours agree, or the difference has been approved.
summary: Write the client's requirements down before costing.
Cost the labour and check the contract's staffing against the costing.
File a signed checklist for every contract accepted.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a contract's staffing be checked against the costing before signing?
options: Because staffing has no effect on price
Because an understaffed price erodes the hourly rate of the work
Because the client usually asks for fewer staff at signing
Because the costing is needed only for large contracts

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item belongs on the contract check sheet?
options: The colour of the crew uniforms
The names of the cleaners' families

knowledgeChecks.question: A client gives a requirement only verbally. What should the operations manager do?
options: Cost it from memory right away
Note it in the diary, then cost it
Ask the crew what they think of it
Confirm it in writing before costing
